Quick summary:
- Redwood published baseline (hosted) for model-redwood-3b: median TTFT 180–220ms, sustained throughput 120 req/s at concurrency 8 (prompt avg 120 tokens), 95th p90 latency < 350ms under warm cache.
- Your earlier trace showed higher TTFT and lower throughput; I want to align on methodology before we dig in.

Proposed immediate steps (we can formalize into the MAP once you confirm):
1) Reproduce test with our playbook (we'll run from our CA region with a warm cache). Owner: Karthik. Target: 2026-06-19.
2) You run an equivalent with your tooling but with cache warm conditions and the same prompt distribution. Owner: Brian. Target: 2026-06-19.
3) Share raw logs and tooling commands (wrk/vegeta/jmeter) + machine specs. Owner: both.
4) If differences persist, we'll run side-by-side in a controlled environment and compare kernel selection, batch sizing, and quantization artifacts. Owner: Marissa + Rishi. Target: 2026-06-22.

Please confirm availability for a 30-min sync today or tomorrow to lock the MAP and the close timeline. I added procurement on CC for contract timing visibility.

Brian — thanks for the quick data. Two obvious differences stand out: your test used Vegeta and cold-cache; our baselines are collected with a warm-KV-cache and our loader uses wrk2 with deterministic inter-arrival times (to avoid bursty fan-in). A few specific points to align on before we escalate:

1) Cache state (cold vs warm): our published TTFT/throughput assumes a warmed KV cache for prefix tokens and attention caches. If your workload is cold on every run you will see higher TTFT and lower throughput. Our recommended warm-up: 200 representative prompts at the target prompt-length distribution executed sequentially.

2) Load generator behavior: Vegeta is rate-based and can create microbursts that change kernel utilization. We typically use wrk2 with rate control and also test with our continuous-batching harness that simulates realistic inter-arrival jitter.

3) Model variant and quantization: you noted redwood-3b-quant — quantization reduces memory but can change kernel selection; confirm whether you used 4-bit or 8-bit quant and whether your runs enabled fallback kernels.

Proposed reproduction plan (I'll own the Redwood side):
- 6/19 09:00–12:00 PT: Redwood runs playbook tests (warm-cache; wrk2; 8 concurrency; 30m steady-state). Deliver: csv of per-request latencies, kernel logs, and process-level GPU metrics.
- 6/19 13:00–17:00 PT: We mirror your Vegeta config (cold and warm runs) and record the same metrics so we can diff.
- 6/20: Side-by-side analysis; if differences persist, trigger a joint side-by-side run on a neutral infra (we can spin up an isolated instance in us-west-2).

Can Marissa/Rishi own the side-by-side and kernel/quantization triage? Marissa, Rishi — can you confirm?

If we hit the expected delta (within 10–15% of our published baseline under aligned methodology), we can commit to the MAP close timeline: final performance sign-off by 6/25 and procurement completion by 6/30. If not, we'll document the root cause and propose mitigations (config changes, model variant recommendation, or dedicated capacity).

Scheduling: Brian, 13:00 PT today works for me for a short sync (30m) to lock owners and timing.

Thanks,
Karthik

Looping in notes from the performance team after a quick read:
- Competitive comparison: we've seen a similar pattern when customers compared us to VendorX — differences often trace to (a) prompt-length distributions, (b) disabled continuous batching on the client side, and (c) different quantization fallbacks.
- Immediate ask for Acme: provide a sample of 10 representative prompts and the tokenization counts so we can replicate the exact token distribution. That will reduce variance in throughput numbers.
- I attached a brief comparison matrix that highlights the knobs to check (batching, seq-len, quant mode, kernel families).

Rishi, can you grab kernel selection logs from our 6/12 runs and add to the drive link Karthik shared? I’ll take point on the matrix and mapping to MR fixes if we find quant fallback issues.

Marissa
Director, Performance & Serving

Subject: MAP: final playbook + owners & close timeline (actionable)

All — finalizing the MAP and owners so Acme procurement has a clear path to a 6/30 close. Below are the discrete tasks, deliverables, and deadlines. Please treat these as the working MAP.

MAP TASKS (owners / due dates):
1) Redwood: Run playbook (warm-cache, wrk2) and share raw CSVs + GPU metrics. Owner: Karthik. Due: 2026-06-19 12:00 PT.
2) Acme: Run Vegeta cold and warm runs with provided warm-up procedure; share raw logs and Vegeta commands. Owner: Brian. Due: 2026-06-19 17:00 PT.
3) Redwood Performance Triage: Kernel selection + quantization diff analysis, side-by-side if needed, and a short remediation proposal. Owners: Marissa, Rishi. Due: 2026-06-22 EOD PT.
4) Executive sign-off packet: consolidated results, recommended config, and statement of expected SLO delta (if any). Owner: Karthik + Marissa. Due: 2026-06-25 EOD PT.
5) Procurement & Contracting: finalize terms and issue PO. Owner: Acme procurement. Target: 2026-06-30.

Acceptance criteria (performance sign-off):
- Under aligned methodology (warm cache, identical prompt distribution, wrk2-style steady arrival), median TTFT within 15% of Redwood baseline and p95 < 2x baseline or a documented mitigation plan.

Escalation plan: If after 6/22 triage we still see >20% deviation, we'll schedule an executive readout (Marissa + Karthik + Brian execs) and discuss Dedicated capacity or reserved GPU tuning for Acme.

Links & attachments: redwood_benchmark_playbook_v1.pdf, compare_matrix.xlsx, hubspot deal link: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345

If no objections, I'll mark the MAP in HubSpot and we’ll proceed. Brian — confirm your run time for 6/19 and I’ll send a calendar invite for the 30-min sync at 13:00 PT.
